response.title: Forecasting directional movements of stock prices for intraday trading using LSTM and random forests
response.task_type: directional movement classification (binary/ternary outperformance vs market)
response.frequency: daily (intraday returns computed at daily resolution)
response.label_definition: Directional movement: whether a stock outperforms the market in terms of intraday returns
data_requirements: S&P 500 constituent stocks from January 1990 until December 2018 sourced from Bloomberg; stocks with zero volume on a given day excluded from trading that day
response.training_protocol: Rolling-window scheme following Krauss et al. (2017) & Fischer & Krauss (2018): 4-year window with 1-year stride; each study period split into ~756 days (~3 years) training and ~252 days (~1 year) trading; 26 study periods with non-overlapping trading parts
response.evaluation_protocol: Out-of-sample backtest over 26 non-overlapping trading periods; on each trading day buy the 10 stocks with highest predicted probability and sell short the 10 with lowest probability, equal monetary weight; benchmark against Krauss et al. (2017) and Fischer & Krauss (2018) single-feature setting
response.cost_assumptions: Returns reported prior to transaction costs
strict_requirements: Buy 10 stocks with highest probability and sell short 10 stocks with lowest probability each trading day
Equal monetary weight across long and short positions
Exclude stocks with zero volume on a given day
unknowns: exact label threshold definition (binary vs ternary)
lookback window length for LSTM input sequence

evidence_spans.quote: We employ both random forests and LSTM networks (more precisely CuDNNLSTM) as training methodologies to analyze their eﬀectiveness in forecasting out-of-sample directional movements of constituent stocks of the S&P 500 from January 1993 till December 2018 for intraday trading.
We introduce a multi-feature setting consisting not only of the returns with respect to the closing prices, but also with respect to the opening prices and intraday returns.

On each trading day, we buy the 10 stocks with the highest probability and sell short the 10 stocks with the lowest probability to outperform the market in terms of intraday returns – all with equal monetary weight.
Our empirical results show that the multi-feature setting provides a daily return, prior to transaction costs, of 0.64% using LSTM networks, and 0.54% using random forests.

we divide the dataset consisting of 29 years starting from January 1990 till December 2018, using a 4-year window and 1-year stride, where each study period is divided into a training period of approximately 756 days (≈ 3 years) and a trading period of approximately 252 days (≈ 1 year). As a consequence, we obtain 26 study periods with non-overlapping trading part.
stocks of the S&P 500 from the period of January 1990 until December 2018 using Bloomberg. For each day, stocks with zero volume were not considered for trading at this day.
All experiments were executed in a NVIDIA Tesla V100 with 30 GB memory. The codes and simulations were implemented using Python 3.6.5 with a dependency of TensorFlow 1.14.0 and scikit-learn 0.20.4.
